newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Cambodia prince urges ASEAN to pressure Hun Sen.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia prince urges ASEAN to pressure Hun Sen.

text.p: Ousted Cambodian co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh said on Monday his country will return to civil war if Southeast Asian governments do not put pressure on his arch-rival Hun Sen.
The prince was ousted last month by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, whose forces are now closing in on Ranariddh's last major stronghold.
"If we do not put pressure on Mr Hun Sen, civil war will erupt," Ranariddh told reporters after talks with Philippine President Ramos.
"Any instability in Cambodia, any fighting in Cambodia will directly affect countries like Thailand, Vietnam and Laos and affect ASEAN as a whole."
Ranariddh is on the fifth leg of a tour of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) seeking support.

ASEAN -- which groups the Philippines, Brunei, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Laos, Burma and Vietnam -- last month postponed Cambodia's entry because of the political turmoil in Phnom Penh.
"I must be allowed in a safe and sound manner...to go back home in my capacity as elected prime minister," he said.
Ranariddh, son of King Norodom Sihanouk, has been replaced as first prime minister by Foreign Minister Ung Huot.
Hun Sen has said that if Ranariddh returned he must face trial for illegal negotiations with the outlawed Khmer Rouge and for smuggling weapons.
Ramos told Ranariddh that the Philippines' attention was now focused on next May's planned general elections in Cambodia and that his country would be willing to help ensure they were fair.

"He called for the participation of all political forces in Cambodia in the poll and urged all Cambodian parties to conclude and observe a ceasefire and end all acts of war and violence," a statement from his office said.
Ranariddh, who has previously refused to announce a unilateral ceasefire, said it was crucial that Hun Sen not be allowed to organise the election alone.
